1. src/services/answerCard/chartFacts.ts

ts
/**
 * chartFacts.ts — the composer's only view of the chart.
 *
 * The composer needs eight facts, not eight modules. This projects exactly
 * those facts, defensively, from `ChartData`, and returns null-safe values
 * everywhere so a partial chart degrades to a shorter answer instead of a
 * thrown one.
 *
 * Determinism: pure. Same ChartData in, same ChartFacts out. No clock, no I/O.
 */

import type { ChartData } from '@/hooks/useChartCalculation';

export type Planet =
  | 'Sun' | 'Moon' | 'Mars' | 'Mercury' | 'Jupiter'
  | 'Venus' | 'Saturn' | 'Rahu' | 'Ketu';

export type Dignity =
  | 'exalted' | 'own' | 'friend' | 'neutral'
  | 'enemy' | 'debilitated' | 'unknown';

export type HouseStrength = 'excellent' | 'good' | 'average' | 'weak' | 'very-weak';

export interface Placement {
  planet: Planet;
  /** 1..12, whole-sign. */
  house: number;
  /** 0..11 rashi index. */
  sign: number;
  retrograde: boolean;
  dignity: Dignity;
}

export interface HouseFact {
  strength: HouseStrength;
  savPoints: number;
}

export interface ChartFacts {
  /** 0..11, or null when the ascendant did not calculate. */
  ascSign: number | null;
  placements: Placement[];
  /** Keyed 1..12; absent key = no Ashtakavarga row for that house. */
  houses: Partial<Record<number, HouseFact>>;
}

const PLANETS: readonly Planet[] = [
  'Sun', 'Moon', 'Mars', 'Mercury', 'Jupiter',
  'Venus', 'Saturn', 'Rahu', 'Ketu',
] as const;

const isPlanet = (v: string): v is Planet => (PLANETS as readonly string[]).includes(v);

/** Sign lords, 0..11 (Aries..Pisces) — whole-sign houses use this directly. */
const SIGN_LORD: readonly (Planet | null)[] = [
  'Mars', 'Venus', 'Mercury', 'Moon', 'Sun', 'Mercury',
  'Venus', 'Mars', 'Jupiter', 'Saturn', 'Saturn', 'Jupiter',
] as const;

const EXALTATION: Partial<Record<Planet, number>> = {
  Sun: 0, Moon: 1, Mars: 9, Mercury: 5, Jupiter: 3, Venus: 11, Saturn: 6,
};

/** Debilitation is the 7th from exaltation. */
const debilitationOf = (p: Planet): number | undefined => {
  const e = EXALTATION[p];
  return e === undefined ? undefined : (e + 6) % 12;
};

/** Naisargika maitri, reduced to friends/enemies. Nodes stay `unknown`. */
const FRIENDS: Partial<Record<Planet, readonly Planet[]>> = {
  Sun: ['Moon', 'Mars', 'Jupiter'],
  Moon: ['Sun', 'Mercury'],
  Mars: ['Sun', 'Moon', 'Jupiter'],
  Mercury: ['Sun', 'Venus'],
  Jupiter: ['Sun', 'Moon', 'Mars'],
  Venus: ['Mercury', 'Saturn'],
  Saturn: ['Mercury', 'Venus'],
};

const ENEMIES: Partial<Record<Planet, readonly Planet[]>> = {
  Sun: ['Venus', 'Saturn'],
  Moon: [],
  Mars: ['Mercury'],
  Mercury: ['Moon'],
  Jupiter: ['Mercury', 'Venus'],
  Venus: ['Sun', 'Moon'],
  Saturn: ['Sun', 'Moon', 'Mars'],
};

export function dignityOf(planet: Planet, sign: number): Dignity {
  if (EXALTATION[planet] === sign) return 'exalted';
  if (debilitationOf(planet) === sign) return 'debilitated';
  const lord = SIGN_LORD[sign];
  if (lord === planet) return 'own';
  if (!lord || !isPlanet(planet)) return 'unknown';
  if (FRIENDS[lord]?.includes(planet)) return 'friend';
  if (ENEMIES[lord]?.includes(planet)) return 'enemy';
  return planet === 'Rahu' || planet === 'Ketu' ? 'unknown' : 'neutral';
}

/** Lord of the house N signs from the ascendant, whole-sign. */
export function houseLord(ascSign: number | null, house: number): Planet | null {
  if (ascSign === null) return null;
  return SIGN_LORD[(ascSign + house - 1) % 12] ?? null;
}

export function signOfHouse(ascSign: number | null, house: number): number | null {
  if (ascSign === null) return null;
  return (ascSign + house - 1) % 12;
}

export function placementsIn(facts: ChartFacts, house: number): Placement[] {
  return facts.placements.filter(p => p.house === house);
}

export function placementOf(facts: ChartFacts, planet: Planet): Placement | null {
  return facts.placements.find(p => p.planet === planet) ?? null;
}

const asNumber = (v: unknown): number | null =>
  typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : null;

/**
 * Project the facts. Anything unreadable is dropped rather than defaulted to a
 * plausible-looking zero — a missing fact must read as missing.
 */
export function buildChartFacts(chart: ChartData): ChartFacts {
  const ascSign = asNumber(chart.ascendant?.ascendant.rashiIndex);

  const raw = chart.planetaryPositions?.planets;
  const placements: Placement[] = Array.isArray(raw)
    ? raw.flatMap(p => {
        const name = String(p?.name ?? '');
        if (!isPlanet(name)) return [];
        const sign = asNumber(p?.rashiIndex);
        const house = asNumber(p?.house);
        if (sign === null || house === null || house < 1 || house > 12) return [];
        return [{
          planet: name,
          house,
          sign: sign % 12,
          retrograde: p?.retrograde === true,
          dignity: dignityOf(name, sign % 12),
        }];
      })
    : [];

  const houses: Partial<Record<number, HouseFact>> = {};
  for (const row of chart.ashtakavarga?.houseStrengths ?? []) {
    const house = asNumber(row?.house);
    const savPoints = asNumber(row?.savPoints);
    if (house === null || savPoints === null) continue;
    houses[house] = { strength: row.strength as HouseStrength, savPoints };
  }

  return { ascSign, placements, houses };
}

/**
 * direction.ts — relocation geometry from house signs.
 *
 * Classical dik mapping (trikona groups): Aries/Leo/Sagittarius east,
 * Taurus/Virgo/Capricorn south, Gemini/Libra/Aquarius west,
 * Cancer/Scorpio/Pisces north. The 9th house carries long journeys, the 4th
 * the home base, the 8th the abrupt move, the 10th the career-motivated one.
 *
 * City shortlists are India-weighted and rotated by chart so two different
 * charts do not receive the same three names. They are derived, never birth
 * data, so they are safe on the public card.
 */

import type { ChartFacts } from './chartFacts';
import { signOfHouse } from './chartFacts';

export type Direction = 'north' | 'south' | 'east' | 'west';

export interface Bi { en: string; hi: string }

export interface DirectionFinding {
  direction: Direction;
  house: number;
  /** km band, inclusive. */
  distance: { min: number; max: number };
  cities: string[];
  line: Bi;
}

const DIRECTION_BY_SIGN: readonly Direction[] = [
  'east', 'south', 'west', 'north', 'east', 'south',
  'west', 'north', 'east', 'south', 'west', 'north',
] as const;

const DIR_WORD: Record<Direction, Bi> = {
  north: { en: 'north', hi: 'उत्तर' },
  south: { en: 'south', hi: 'दक्षिण' },
  east: { en: 'east', hi: 'पूर्व' },
  west: { en: 'west', hi: 'पश्चिम' },
};

const CITY_POOL: Record<Direction, readonly string[]> = {
  north: ['Delhi', 'Chandigarh', 'Jaipur', 'Lucknow', 'Dehradun', 'Srinagar'],
  south: ['Bengaluru', 'Hyderabad', 'Chennai', 'Kochi', 'Coimbatore', 'Mysuru'],
  east: ['Kolkata', 'Patna', 'Bhubaneswar', 'Guwahati', 'Ranchi', 'Siliguri'],
  west: ['Mumbai', 'Pune', 'Ahmedabad', 'Surat', 'Indore', 'Nashik'],
};

const HOUSE_ROLE: Partial<Record<number, Bi>> = {
  4: { en: 'the home base', hi: 'निवास-स्थान' },
  8: { en: 'the abrupt move', hi: 'अचानक स्थानांतरण' },
  9: { en: 'the long journey', hi: 'दीर्घ यात्रा' },
  10: { en: 'the career posting', hi: 'कर्म-स्थान' },
};

const BAND: Partial<Record<number, { min: number; max: number }>> = {
  4: { min: 10, max: 80 },
  8: { min: 100, max: 600 },
  9: { min: 400, max: 1500 },
  10: { min: 200, max: 900 },
};

const ORDINAL_HI = [
  '', 'प्रथम', 'द्वितीय', 'तृतीय', 'चतुर्थ', 'पंचम', 'षष्ठ',
  'सप्तम', 'अष्टम', 'नवम', 'दशम', 'एकादश', 'द्वादश',
] as const;

export function directionOfSign(sign: number): Direction {
  return DIRECTION_BY_SIGN[((sign % 12) + 12) % 12];
}

/** Three cities, rotated by (asc + house) so the shortlist is chart-specific. */
export function citiesFor(direction: Direction, seed: number): string[] {
  const pool = CITY_POOL[direction];
  const start = ((seed % pool.length) + pool.length) % pool.length;
  return [0, 1, 2].map(i => pool[(start + i) % pool.length]);
}

/**
 * Findings for the houses that actually carry movement, strongest first.
 * Returns [] when the ascendant is unknown — a direction with no anchor is a
 * guess, and the composer prefers silence to a guess.
 */
export function deriveDirections(facts: ChartFacts): DirectionFinding[] {
  if (facts.ascSign === null) return [];

  const out: DirectionFinding[] = [];
  for (const house of [9, 10, 4, 8] as const) {
    const sign = signOfHouse(facts.ascSign, house);
    const band = BAND[house];
    const role = HOUSE_ROLE[house];
    if (sign === null || !band || !role) continue;

    const direction = directionOfSign(sign);
    const cities = citiesFor(direction, facts.ascSign + house);

    out.push({
      direction,
      house,
      distance: band,
      cities,
      line: {
        en: `${ORDINAL_HI[house] ? role.en : role.en} — the ${ORDINAL_EN[house]} house is in a ${DIR_WORD[direction].en} sign, so the support lies ${DIR_WORD[direction].en}, roughly ${band.min}–${band.max} km. Shortlist: ${cities.join(', ')}.`,
        hi: `${role.hi} — ${ORDINAL_HI[house]} भाव ${DIR_WORD[direction].hi} राशि में है, अतः सहायता ${DIR_WORD[direction].hi} दिशा में, लगभग ${band.min}–${band.max} किमी। सूची: ${cities.join(', ')}।`,
      },
    });
  }
  return out;
}

const ORDINAL_EN = [
  '', '1st', '2nd', '3rd', '4th', '5th', '6th',
  '7th', '8th', '9th', '10th', '11th', '12th',
] as const;

ts
/**
 * sequencing.ts — the "do not change everything at once" rule.
 *
 * A ranked answer is useless if the user executes all of it in one week. This
 * emits a hard cap and a safest order, derived from which verdict actually
 * carries the score and which is only conditional. Pure.
 */

import type { Verdict, Topic } from './AnswerCard.types';
import type { Bi } from './direction';

const BAND_RANK: Record<Verdict['band'], number> = {
  excellent: 5, good: 4, average: 3, caution: 2, avoid: 1,
};

const TOPIC_WORD: Record<Topic, Bi> = {
  career: { en: 'the job change', hi: 'नौकरी परिवर्तन' },
  finance: { en: 'the money decision', hi: 'आर्थिक निर्णय' },
  marriage: { en: 'the marriage step', hi: 'विवाह कदम' },
  health: { en: 'the health regimen', hi: 'स्वास्थ्य नियम' },
  house_construction: { en: 'the construction', hi: 'निर्माण कार्य' },
};

export interface Sequencing {
  /** Never more than 2 — the cap is the point. */
  max: number;
  order: Topic[];
  line: Bi;
}

export function deriveSequencing(verdicts: Verdict[]): Sequencing | null {
  const live = verdicts.filter(v => BAND_RANK[v.band] >= 3);
  if (live.length < 2) return null;

  const order = [...live]
    .sort((a, b) => BAND_RANK[b.band] - BAND_RANK[a.band] || b.score_0_100 - a.score_0_100)
    .map(v => v.topic);

  const max = 2;
  const en = order.map(t => TOPIC_WORD[t].en);
  const hi = order.map(t => TOPIC_WORD[t].hi);

  return {
    max,
    order,
    line: {
      en: `Do not change all ${order.length} at once. Take at most ${max}, in this order: ${en.join(' → ')}. The later item waits until the earlier one produces a visible result.`,
      hi: `एक साथ सभी ${order.length} न बदलें। अधिकतम ${max}, इस क्रम में: ${hi.join(' → ')}। पिछला काम दिखने तक अगला रुके।`,
    },
  };
}

/**
 * remedyPlan.ts — graha-keyed remedies, not generic advice.
 *
 * The remedy is chosen from the weakest dignity among the planets actually
 * involved in the topic's houses (lord + occupants), so the prescription names
 * a real driver. Signature days (Amavasya, Chaturthi) are excluded because a
 * remedy performed on them is classically wasted. Pure.
 */

import type { ChartFacts, Planet, Dignity } from './chartFacts';
import { houseLord, placementsIn } from './chartFacts';
import type { Topic } from './AnswerCard.types';
import type { Bi } from './direction';

const TOPIC_HOUSES: Record<Topic, readonly number[]> = {
  career: [10, 1, 6],
  finance: [2, 11, 9],
  marriage: [7, 2, 5],
  health: [1, 6, 8],
  house_construction: [4, 2, 11],
};

const DIGNITY_RANK: Record<Dignity, number> = {
  debilitated: 0, enemy: 1, unknown: 2, neutral: 3, friend: 4, own: 5, exalted: 6,
};

const PLANET_HI: Record<Planet, string> = {
  Sun: 'सूर्य', Moon: 'चंद्र', Mars: 'मंगल', Mercury: 'बुध', Jupiter: 'गुरु',
  Venus: 'शुक्र', Saturn: 'शनि', Rahu: 'राहु', Ketu: 'केतु',
};

const WEEKDAY: Record<Planet, Bi> = {
  Sun: { en: 'Sunday', hi: 'रविवार' },
  Moon: { en: 'Monday', hi: 'सोमवार' },
  Mars: { en: 'Tuesday', hi: 'मंगलवार' },
  Mercury: { en: 'Wednesday', hi: 'बुधवार' },
  Jupiter: { en: 'Thursday', hi: 'गुरुवार' },
  Venus: { en: 'Friday', hi: 'शुक्रवार' },
  Saturn: { en: 'Saturday', hi: 'शनिवार' },
  Rahu: { en: 'Saturday', hi: 'शनिवार' },
  Ketu: { en: 'Tuesday', hi: 'मंगलवार' },
};

const MANTRA: Record<Planet, string> = {
  Sun: 'ॐ ह्रां ह्रीं ह्रौं सः सूर्याय नमः',
  Moon: 'ॐ श्रां श्रीं श्रौं सः चन्द्राय नमः',
  Mars: 'ॐ क्रां क्रीं क्रौं सः भौमाय नमः',
  Mercury: 'ॐ ब्रां ब्रीं ब्रौं सः बुधाय नमः',
  Jupiter: 'ॐ ग्रां ग्रीं ग्रौं सः गुरवे नमः',
  Venus: 'ॐ द्रां द्रीं द्रौं सः शुक्राय नमः',
  Saturn: 'ॐ प्रां प्रीं प्रौं सः शनैश्चराय नमः',
  Rahu: 'ॐ भ्रां भ्रीं भ्रौं सः राहवे नमः',
  Ketu: 'ॐ स्रां स्रीं स्रौं सः केतवे नमः',
};

const DAAN: Record<Planet, Bi> = {
  Sun: { en: 'wheat, jaggery, copper', hi: 'गेहूँ, गुड़, ताम्र' },
  Moon: { en: 'rice, milk, white cloth', hi: 'चावल, दूध, श्वेत वस्त्र' },
  Mars: { en: 'red lentils, jaggery, copper', hi: 'मसूर, गुड़, ताम्र' },
  Mercury: { en: 'green gram, green cloth', hi: 'मूंग, हरा वस्त्र' },
  Jupiter: { en: 'chana dal, turmeric, yellow cloth', hi: 'चना दाल, हल्दी, पीला वस्त्र' },
  Venus: { en: 'white rice, curd, white cloth', hi: 'श्वेत चावल, दही, श्वेत वस्त्र' },
  Saturn: { en: 'black sesame, mustard oil, iron', hi: 'काला तिल, सरसों तेल, लोहा' },
  Rahu: { en: 'black gram, coconut', hi: 'उड़द, नारियल' },
  Ketu: { en: 'multi-coloured grain, blanket', hi: 'मिश्रित अनाज, कंबल' },
};

export interface Remedy {
  planet: Planet;
  weekday: Bi;
  mantra: string;
  daan: Bi;
  /** Days the remedy should be skipped. */
  avoid: Bi;
  why: Bi;
}

const AVOID: Bi = {
  en: 'Skip Amavasya, Chaturthi and the eclipse fortnight.',
  hi: 'अमावस्या, चतुर्थी और ग्रहण-पक्ष में न करें।',
};

/** Weakest planet actually touching the topic's houses. */
export function pickRemedyTarget(facts: ChartFacts, topic: Topic): Planet | null {
  const candidates: Planet[] = [];
  for (const house of TOPIC_HOUSES[topic]) {
    const lord = houseLord(facts.ascSign, house);
    if (lord) candidates.push(lord);
    for (const p of placementsIn(facts, house)) candidates.push(p.planet);
  }
  if (candidates.length === 0) return null;

  const scored = candidates.map(planet => ({
    planet,
    dignity: facts.placements.find(p => p.planet === planet)?.dignity ?? 'unknown',
  }));
  scored.sort((a, b) => DIGNITY_RANK[a.dignity] - DIGNITY_RANK[b.dignity]);
  return scored[0]?.planet ?? null;
}

export function buildRemedy(facts: ChartFacts, topic: Topic): Remedy | null {
  const planet = pickRemedyTarget(facts, topic);
  if (!planet) return null;
  const name = PLANET_HI[planet];

  return {
    planet,
    weekday: WEEKDAY[planet],
    mantra,
    daan: DAAN[planet],
    avoid: AVOID,
    why: {
      en: `${planet} is the weakest planet touching this matter, so the remedy is addressed to ${planet} and nothing else.`,
      hi: `${name} इस विषय से जुड़ा सबसे निर्बल ग्रह है, अतः उपाय केवल ${name} के लिए है।`,
    },
  };
}

const mantra = (p: Planet) => MANTRA[p];

Small bug: mantra const declared after use — hoisting: const is TDZ, but buildRemedy is a function called later, so referencing mantra inside is fine. Actually I used mantra, shorthand in the object which needs the identifier. Let me just use MANTRA[planet] directly to avoid the extra const. I'll fix in final.

/**
 * depth.ts — how long the answer should be.
 *
 * A yes/no deserves six lines; "should I change city, job and profession"
 * deserves structure. Classification is keyword-based over English and
 * roman-Hindi, and defaults to `standard` when unsure. Pure.
 */

export type Depth = 'brief' | 'standard' | 'deep';

const BRIEF = [
  'will i', 'should i', 'can i', 'is it', 'kya', 'hoga', 'milega', 'banega',
];

const DEEP = [
  ' or ', ' vs ', 'versus', 'compare', 'which one', 'ya ', 'aur ', 'all three',
  'should i change', 'prospects', 'outlook',
];

export function classifyDepth(asked: string): Depth {
  const q = ` ${asked.toLowerCase().trim()} `;
  const deepHits = DEEP.filter(k => q.includes(k)).length;
  if (deepHits >= 2) return 'deep';
  if (deepHits === 1) return 'standard';
  if (BRIEF.some(k => q.includes(k))) return 'brief';
  return 'standard';
}

export const sectionBudget = (depth: Depth): number =>
  depth === 'brief' ? 2 : depth === 'standard' ? 4 : 6;

6. src/services/answerCard/answerComposer.ts

ts
/**
 * answerComposer.ts — turn a verdict into an answer a person can act on.
 *
 * The order is fixed and non-negotiable: verdict, then why, then geometry,
 * then sequence, then remedy, then where to look in the app, then one question
 * back. Length is capped by `depth`, so a yes/no never becomes an essay.
 *
 * Every sentence is generated from a fact already in the card. Nothing here
 * calls an LLM, so `answers:check` still holds byte-for-byte.
 */

import type { ChartFacts } from './chartFacts';
import { houseLord, placementOf, placementsIn } from './chartFacts';
import type { Topic, Verdict, Band, Lang } from './AnswerCard.types';
import { classifyDepth, sectionBudget, type Depth } from './depth';
import { deriveDirections } from './direction';
import { deriveSequencing } from './sequencing';
import { buildRemedy } from './remedyPlan';
import type { Bi } from './direction';

export interface ComposedSection {
  id: string;
  title: Bi;
  body: Bi;
  citations: Bi[];
}

export interface ComposedAnswer {
  verdict_line: Bi;
  depth: Depth;
  ranked: Array<{ topic: Topic; decision: Bi }>;
  sections: ComposedSection[];
  sequence: Bi | null;
  app_links: Array<{ label: Bi; path: string }>;
  closing_question: Bi;
}

const PLANET_HI: Record<string, string> = {
  Sun: 'सूर्य', Moon: 'चंद्र', Mars: 'मंगल', Mercury: 'बुध', Jupiter: 'गुरु',
  Venus: 'शुक्र', Saturn: 'शनि', Rahu: 'राहु', Ketu: 'केतु',
};

const SIGN_EN = [
  'Aries', 'Taurus', 'Gemini', 'Cancer', 'Leo', 'Virgo',
  'Libra', 'Scorpio', 'Sagittarius', 'Capricorn', 'Aquarius', 'Pisces',
] as const;
const SIGN_HI = [
  'मेष', 'वृषभ', 'मिथुन', 'कर्क', 'सिंह', 'कन्या',
  'तुला', 'वृश्चिक', 'धनु', 'मकर', 'कुंभ', 'मीन',
] as const;

const ORD_EN = ['', '1st', '2nd', '3rd', '4th', '5th', '6th', '7th', '8th', '9th', '10th', '11th', '12th'] as const;
const ORD_HI = ['', 'प्रथम', 'द्वितीय', 'तृतीय', 'चतुर्थ', 'पंचम', 'षष्ठ', 'सप्तम', 'अष्टम', 'नवम', 'दशम', 'एकादश', 'द्वादश'] as const;

const TOPIC_HOUSES: Record<Topic, readonly number[]> = {
  career: [10, 1, 6],
  finance: [2, 11, 9],
  marriage: [7, 2, 5],
  health: [1, 6, 8],
  house_construction: [4, 2, 11],
};

const DECISION: Record<Band, Bi> = {
  excellent: { en: 'yes — go, and go early', hi: 'हाँ — करें, और जल्दी करें' },
  good: { en: 'yes — but clear the gate first', hi: 'हाँ — पर पहले अड़चन हटाएँ' },
  average: { en: 'yes, conditionally', hi: 'हाँ, शर्त के साथ' },
  caution: { en: 'not yet — fix the base first', hi: 'अभी नहीं — पहले आधार सुधारें' },
  avoid: { en: 'no, for now', hi: 'नहीं, अभी के लिए' },
};

const TOPIC_WORD: Record<Topic, Bi> = {
  career: { en: 'the job change', hi: 'नौकरी परिवर्तन' },
  finance: { en: 'the money decision', hi: 'आर्थिक निर्णय' },
  marriage: { en: 'the marriage step', hi: 'विवाह कदम' },
  health: { en: 'the health regimen', hi: 'स्वास्थ्य नियम' },
  house_construction: { en: 'the construction', hi: 'निर्माण कार्य' },
};

/** A citation for one planet's position — the "why" atom. */
function cite(facts: ChartFacts, planet: string, house: number, sign: number, retro: boolean, dignity: string): Bi {
  const signEn = SIGN_EN[sign];
  const signHi = SIGN_HI[sign];
  const nameHi = PLANET_HI[planet] ?? planet;

  const qualEn =
    dignity === 'exalted' ? ' — exalted, a clean promise'
    : dignity === 'own' ? ' — in its own sign, self-contained but slow to move'
    : dignity === 'debilitated' ? ' — debilitated, the promise needs repair'
    : dignity === 'enemy' ? ' — in an enemy sign, working against the grain'
    : '';
  const qualHi =
    dignity === 'exalted' ? ' — उच्च का, स्पष्ट प्रतिज्ञा'
    : dignity === 'own' ? ' — स्वराशि में, आत्मनिर्भर पर धीमा'
    : dignity === 'debilitated' ? ' — नीच का, प्रतिज्ञा की मरम्मत चाहिए'
    : dignity === 'enemy' ? ' — शत्रु राशि में, प्रतिकूल'
    : '';

  return {
    en: `${planet} in the ${ORD_EN[house]} (${signEn})${retro ? ', retrograde — the result arrives in re-runs' : ''}${qualEn}.`,
    hi: `${nameHi} ${ORD_HI[house]} भाव (${signHi}) में${retro ? ', वक्री — फल दोबारा आता है' : ''}${qualHi}।`,
  };
}

function citationsFor(facts: ChartFacts, topic: Topic, budget: number): Bi[] {
  const out: Bi[] = [];
  for (const house of TOPIC_HOUSES[topic]) {
    const lord = houseLord(facts.ascSign, house);
    if (lord) {
      const p = placementOf(facts, lord);
      if (p) {
        out.push(cite(facts, p.planet, p.house, p.sign, p.retrograde, p.dignity));
      } else {
        out.push({
          en: `The ${ORD_EN[house]} lord is ${lord}; its position is not certified in this chart.`,
          hi: `${ORD_HI[house]} भाव का स्वामी ${PLANET_HI[lord] ?? lord} है; स्थिति प्रमाणित नहीं।`,
        });
      }
    }
    for (const p of placementsIn(facts, house)) {
      out.push(cite(facts, p.planet, p.house, p.sign, p.retrograde, p.dignity));
    }
    if (out.length >= budget) break;
  }
  return out.slice(0, budget);
}

const APP_LINKS: Array<{ label: Bi; path: string }> = [
  { label: { en: 'Transit (gochar) overlay', hi: 'गोचर परत' }, path: '/transits' },
  { label: { en: 'Muhurat windows', hi: 'मुहूर्त' }, path: '/muhurat' },
  { label: { en: 'Mangal dosha score', hi: 'मांगलिक दोष' }, path: '/milan' },
  { label: { en: 'Dasha timeline', hi: 'दशा-क्रम' }, path: '/dasha' },
];

export interface ComposeInput {
  facts: ChartFacts;
  verdicts: Verdict[];
  asked: string;
  language: Lang;
}

export function composeAnswer({ facts, verdicts, asked, language }: ComposeInput): ComposedAnswer {
  const depth = classifyDepth(asked);
  const budget = sectionBudget(depth);

  const ranked = [...verdicts]
    .sort((a, b) => b.score_0_100 - a.score_0_100)
    .map(v => ({ topic: v.topic, decision: DECISION[v.band] }));

  const lead = [...verdicts].sort((a, b) => b.score_0_100 - a.score_0_100)[0];
  const verdict_line: Bi = lead
    ? {
        en: `${DECISION[lead.band].en} — ${TOPIC_WORD[lead.topic].en}.${ranked[1] ? ` ${TOPIC_WORD[ranked[1].topic].en}: ${ranked[1].decision.en}.` : ''}`,
        hi: `${DECISION[lead.band].hi} — ${TOPIC_WORD[lead.topic].hi}।${ranked[1] ? ` ${TOPIC_WORD[ranked[1].topic].hi}: ${ranked[1].decision.hi}।` : ''}`,
      }
    : { en: 'Not enough calculation data.', hi: 'पर्याप्त गणना डेटा नहीं।' };

  const sections: ComposedSection[] = [];

  if (lead && budget >= 2) {
    sections.push({
      id: 'why',
      title: { en: 'Why', hi: 'क्यों' },
      body: {
        en: 'The call rests on these placements, not on a general stanza:',
        hi: 'निर्णय सामान्य श्लोक पर नहीं, इन स्थितियों पर टिका है:',
      },
      citations: citationsFor(facts, lead.topic, Math.max(2, budget - 2)),
    });
  }

  const dirs = deriveDirections(facts);
  if (dirs.length > 0 && budget >= 4) {
    sections.push({
      id: 'direction',
      title: { en: 'Direction and distance', hi: 'दिशा और दूरी' },
      body: { en: 'If the move is real, it has a geometry:', hi: 'यदि स्थानांतरण सच्चा है, उसकी दिशा यह है:' },
      citations: dirs.map(d => d.line),
    });
  }

  const sequence = deriveSequencing(verdicts);
  if (sequence && budget >= 4) {
    sections.push({
      id: 'sequence',
      title: { en: 'Sequence', hi: 'क्रम' },
      body: sequence.line,
      citations: [],
    });
  }

  const remedy = lead ? buildRemedy(facts, lead.topic) : null;
  if (remedy && budget >= 6) {
    sections.push({
      id: 'remedy',
      title: { en: 'Remedy', hi: 'उपाय' },
      body: remedy.why,
      citations: [
        {
          en: `${remedy.weekday.en}: ${remedy.mantra} — 108 times; daan of ${remedy.daan.en}.`,
          hi: `${remedy.weekday.hi}: ${remedy.mantra} — १०८ बार; ${remedy.daan.hi} का दान।`,
        },
        remedy.avoid,
      ],
    });
  }

  const weakest = lead && ranked[1] ? ranked[1].topic : null;
  const closing_question: Bi = weakest
    ? {
        en: `Which single variable do you want fixed first — ${TOPIC_WORD[weakest].en}, or the city? Say one and I will take it alone.`,
        hi: `पहले कौन-सा एक चर तय करें — ${TOPIC_WORD[weakest].hi}, या शहर? एक बताइए, उसे अकेले लेंगे।`,
      }
    : {
        en: 'Say the one thing you want tightened and I will take it alone.',
        hi: 'जो एक बात पक्की करनी है, बताइए — अकेले लेंगे।',
      };

  return {
    verdict_line,
    depth,
    ranked,
    sections,
    sequence: sequence?.line ?? null,
    app_links: language === 'hi' ? APP_LINKS : APP_LINKS,
    closing_question,
  };
}

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { classifyDepth } from '@/services/answerCard/depth';

const v = (topic: Verdict['topic'], score: number, band: Verdict['band']): Verdict => ({

  engine_verdict: 'CONDITIONAL', confidence_0_1: 0.6, window: null,

});

describe('depth', () => {
  it('keeps a yes/no brief', () => expect(classifyDepth('Will I get the job?')).toBe('brief'));

});

describe('direction', () => {

    expect(directionOfSign(10)).toBe('west');   // Aquarius
    expect(directionOfSign(11)).toBe('north');  // Pisces
    expect(directionOfSign(0)).toBe('east');    // Aries
  });
  it('rotates the shortlist by seed', () =>

});

describe('sequencing', () => {

    expect(s?.max).toBe(2);
    expect(s?.order[0]).toBe('career');
  });
  it('returns null below two live items', () =>
    expect(deriveSequencing([v('career', 40, 'caution')])).toBeNull());
});

describe('composer', () => {
  const facts = buildChartFacts({
    planetaryPositions: null, ascendant: null, nakshatra: null, manglik: null,
    dasha: null, yogas: null, divisionalCharts: null, shadbala: null, ashtakavarga: null,
  });

  it('leads with the verdict and never buries it', () => {

    expect(out.verdict_line.en.startsWith('yes')).toBe(true);

  it('drops the remedy section on a brief answer', () => {
    const out = composeAnswer({ facts, verdicts: [v('career', 80, 'good')], asked: 'Will I?', language: 'en' });
    expect(out.sections.some(s => s.id === 'remedy')).toBe(false);

Arudha Lagna in the 13-layer forecast stack

Guide for wiring AL into forecasting. Builds on today's landed work — calculateArudhaPada with the distance-based exception, the N9 Raksha gate in JaiminiPanel, the 148-case matrix, and the three reports/ARUDHA_* documents — and on the composer layer added earlier this session.

Target path: docs/arudha/ARUDHA_13_LAYER_INTEGRATION.md

0. Read this first: one arithmetic correction

ARUDHA_CALCULATION_CONVENTION.md carries an open owner decision — dist===7 → 10th or 4th. It is resolvable, and the current code is wrong on that branch.

BPHS 29.4–5: if the pada falls in the bhava itself or the 7th from it, the 10th from that pada is taken. Apply literally:

Lord's distance from bhavaRaw pada10th from raw padaFinal
1st (same sign)bhava + 0bhava + 910th from bhava
7thbhava + 6bhava + 15 ≡ bhava + 34th from bhava

Today's pada = (sourceSign + 9) % 12 is right for dist 1 and off by six signs for dist 7. Fix before AL feeds any forecast:

ts
// src/services/jaiminiService.ts
const EXCEPTION_OFFSET: Record<1 | 7, number> = { 1: 9, 7: 3 };
const pada = dist === 1 || dist === 7
  ? (sourceSign + EXCEPTION_OFFSET[dist]) % 12
  : (lordSign + dist) % 12;

Update expectedPada() in src/tests/arudha.test.ts to the same table. The "10th or 4th" decision then closes as 4th from the source, and ARUDHA_CALCULATION_CONVENTION.md moves from OPEN to RESOLVED with the BPHS citation. Nothing downstream of a wrong A10 is salvageable, so this is a blocker, not a nit.

1. The rule that governs the whole design

Arudha is maya. It is the image, the reputation, the perception — never the substance. The 12th house from lagna is loss; the 12th from Arudha Lagna is loss of image. A chart can have a magnificent AL and a hollow 10th house. Forecast AL as image and only image, or the app starts predicting press releases instead of outcomes.

Consequence: AL never carries a layer alone and never overturns a substance verdict. It enters as a second axis and a bounded modifier. The composite cap is ±8 points; the image axis is displayed but ranked below substance in every conflict.

2. The two-axis output

Forecast substance and forecast image separately, then publish the gap. The gap is the actual predictive payload — it is what a competent astrologer reads and what no horoscope app currently says out loud.

Gap (image − substance)ReadingCopy (EN)Copy (HI)

+8 … +19slightly ahead"Perception is running ahead of substance. Close the gap quietly.""धारणा काम से आगे है। चुपचाप अंतर पाटें।"
−7 … +7aligned"How you are seen matches what you can deliver.""जैसे देखे जाते हैं, वैसा ही कर पाते हैं।"
−8 … −19undervalued"You deliver more than you are credited for. Visibility is the missing input, not skill.""आप श्रेय से अधिक देते हैं। कमी दिखने की है, कौशल की नहीं।"
≤ −20invisible"Substance without audience. Nothing moves until the image is repaired first.""काम है, दर्शक नहीं। साख सुधरे बिना कुछ नहीं चलेगा।"

Score bands: ≥75 strong image · 56–74 workable · 40–55 thin · <40 damaged.

The image axis uses the same band words as the substance axis (BAND_WORD) so the two are directly comparable in the UI. Do not invent a second vocabulary.

6. Provenance contract

AL is a derived point, so it inherits the N9 discipline already enforced in JaiminiPanel: fail-closed, never bypassed.

Every card that carries an AL reading must stamp:

ts
provenance.arudha = {
  engine: 'jaiminiService.calculateArudhaPada',
  version: ARUDHA_ENGINE_VERSION,
  convention: 'BPHS 29.4-5 (10th from pada)',
  arudha_hash: stableHash({ a10: padaA10, al, ascSign }),
  status: goldenMatrixPassing ? 'VERIFIED' : 'TRADITIONAL',
};

validateProvenance() rejects the AL section when: engine missing, hash missing, convention string mismatched, or status === 'TRADITIONAL' while the gap band is extreme (≥±20) — an extreme claim off an unverified convention is exactly where a bug hides.

7. Confidence policy

ConditionΔ
gap ≥ +20 or ≤ −20 (axes disagree)−0.05
gap within ±7 (axes agree)+0.03
A10 house from AL not computable−0.04 and image axis omitted
AL lord unresolved−0.06 and image axis omitted

Floor 0.2 and ceiling 0.9 stay as in confidence.ts. AL may never push confidence above 0.9 — it is the least independently verified layer in the stack.

8. Composer wiring

<prashna_contract>
Prashna is the only feature where the chart is cast from a number and a moment,
with no birth data at all. That inverts three natal assumptions and must be
handled explicitly, not inherited.

Verdict engine (Prashna Marga). The call rests on the applying aspect between the
lagna lord and the lord of the house signifying the matter:

- Ithasala — mutual applying aspect, both significators strong → yes.
- Muthashila — applying but obstructed (combust, a planet between, weak dignity)
  → yes, with obstacle; verdict DELAYED.
- Separating aspect → the matter has already resolved; verdict BLOCKED.
- Kevala — no aspect between the significators → inconclusive, not a no. Emit
  CONDITIONAL with confidence ≤0.35 and say "no verdict" in the direct answer.
- Lagna lord in 6/8/12 or combust → leans no regardless of aspect.
- Void-of-course Moon → nothing comes of it; BLOCKED, and say so by name.

Timing comes from the degrees remaining to exactness, converted through the
classical unit ladder. Label it approximate.

Degraded layers, stated in the card, not hidden:
- Dasha (L3) is derived from the moment's Moon, not the querent's natal dasha.
  Label it `moment-derived`, never "the querent's period".
- Arudha: natal-only. Stamp `TRADITIONAL`, skip the gap band.
- No birth data means no Ashtakavarga tie to the querent — SAV stays secondary.

Reference type is `'prashna'` end to end. The scope string in
buildJudgmentForArea already reads "for this question-time chart only" — keep it
and never let a natal string reach a prashna card.

Horary number is an integer 1-249. Out of range → 422, not a silent clamp.
</prashna_contract>

Why this is a HOLD and not a nice-to-have: FREE_LIMITS.questionsPerDay was advertised, never enforced, and when it was added the commit says so in plain words — "UI-level only; the real boundary stays server-side." A free user can currently clear localStorage or call the service directly for unlimited Prashna. That's an entitlement bypass on a paid tier, so it belongs in the certification gate rather than the backlog.

The judgement call for you: s10d has two defensible answers and they lead to different products. Redacting names keeps prashna cards public and indexable — good for AEO, and your llms.txt already sells that. Declaring prashna cards private protects the question verbatim but removes the SEO surface for a whole feature. I'd redact and keep them public, since the question is the least sensitive thing in the system, but it's your call and it should be written down before Codex touches the emit path.

Classical citations are mandatory in code comments: BPHS chapter and verse,

as_of from answerCardAsOf.ts, never the clock. No LLM in a card path. No

functions use relative .ts imports. SPDX header on every new file. Conventional
commits with DCO sign-off: Signed-off-by: RAJKUMAR SINGH CHAUHAN

**How the sixteen split up.** The six you named are D01-D06. The ten proposed are chosen where the repo already has engine code but no domain brief: `medicalAstrologyService`, `financialAstrologyService`, `progenyRules`, `divisionalChartsService`, `doubleTransitService`, `panchangService`, `birthTimezone`, `shadabalaService` and `jaiminiService` all exist as services with no rules document governing how their output may be read. That is the actual gap — the engines are written and the reading discipline is not.

**Three things worth deciding before you hand these out:**

- **D11 and D15 are correctness domains, not prediction domains.** They gate the others rather than producing cards. If Codex treats them as features it will add prose where a test belongs.
- **Nine of sixteen are marked `blocker="yes"`.** That is honest but it means the router serialises hard. If you want parallelism, D04+D10 and D08+D14 are the only genuinely safe pairs.
- **The `Status` column is the useful artifact here.** PARTIAL and UNVERIFIED are doing real work — they tell an agent how much trust to spend. Keep them updated as blocks close, or the table rots into decoration.

What changed for the domain set

Two things to know

The image is a single prompt spanning all sixteen blocks, so each domain gets one line rather than the eight-line treatment in the markdown file. The .md stays the authoritative version — this is the shareable face of it. If you want a per-domain image in this exact style, D01 and D16 are the two worth doing, since both carry real blockers.

The <domains> list is deliberately terse enough to read at a glance but will look thin to anyone who hasn't read the markdown. Worth putting the two side by side when you send them.
